articles.headline: Iran conflict pushes Brent crude above $85, Hormuz transit disrupted
articles.analysis: Oil price surge inflates Pakistan's import bill. PSO margins compress — govt caps retail prices while crude input costs rise. PPL/OGDC benefit from higher wellhead gas prices but circular debt delays cash realization.

articles.headline: SBP holds policy rate at 10.5%
articles.analysis: Rate pause preserves bank NIMs. UBL/HBL/MCB earn spread on 10.5% lending vs 7-8% deposit costs. MEBL less affected — Islamic profit-sharing adjusts with lag.

articles.headline: Pakistan IT exports surge 23% YoY
articles.analysis: SYS captures ~15% of listed IT export revenue. Each 1% PKR depreciation adds ~₨0.4 to EPS through translation gains.

articles.headline: KSE-100 corrects 10% from ATH
articles.analysis: Broad correction after 65% rally. High-beta stocks (UBL β1.49, PPL β1.45) fell 15-18%. Low-beta MEBL/MCB held better.

articles.headline: PKR weakens to 282/USD
articles.analysis: SYS benefits (USD revenues). PSO import bill rises. LUCK cement exports become more competitive.

articles.headline: CPEC Phase II: $2.3B projects approved
articles.analysis: ML-1 railway and motorways consume ~2M tons cement annually. LUCK holds 15% northern market share. PAEL supplies switchgear.

articles.headline: IMF review: circular debt resolution progressing
articles.analysis: Govt owes PSO ~₨300B — each ₨50B recovery unlocks working capital. PPL/OGDC/SNGP similarly exposed.

articles.headline: Remittances hit $3.29B in February
articles.analysis: Higher remittances = more CASA deposits = lower funding costs for banks. UBL Middle East branches capture flows directly.

articles.headline: NDMA warns monsoon 26% above average
articles.analysis: 2022 floods disrupted cement dispatches for 2 months and damaged wellhead infrastructure. Similar risk ahead.

articles.headline: Engro subsidiary reports strong fertilizer demand
articles.analysis: EFERT dividend is 60% of ENGROH income. Strong Rabi urea offtake signals healthy payout.

news.marketSummary: KSE-100 is consolidating about 10% below its January high as oil above $85 and a softer rupee weigh on importers. The SBP hold at 10.5%, steady IMF progress on circular debt and record remittances keep the medium-term picture constructive for banks and E&Ps.
news.topAction: Your PSO position is overweight and exposed to the oil spike: trim it, and use this month's budget to add to OGDC and PPL rather than chasing more PSO.

advice.summary: The market is digesting a 10% correction driven by oil and geopolitics, not by weaker earnings. Keep buying gradually: tilt this month’s ₨50,000 toward cheap, cash-generative E&Ps and a dividend bank, and keep a small cash buffer in case the Hormuz situation deepens the pullback.
